page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv4 server family. It runs on the x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor with a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz. The server is configured with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (8 physical cores with 2 threads per core) and a memory allocation of 504.0 GB, yielding 31.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It features 2458 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Performance benchmarks place this server consistently in the average range across multiple categories. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU performance score of 1486.38 and a multi-core score of 15092.71. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 842.48 GB/sec and a large block uncached speed of 101.42 GB/sec. In database-related workloads, the server handles 14.55 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 7126.2 on PassMark database operations. For language model tasks, it processes 135M model prompts at 872.77 tokens per second, though performance drops to a weak 29.58 tokens per second for 7B model prompt processing.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and built-in 2458 GB local SSD, the E64-16ds_v4 offers high resource density for memory-bound applications without requiring a proportional increase in compute licensing costs. This makes it highly cost-efficient for large relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and data analytics pipelines. However, the lack of a GPU and the average single-core CPU performance make it less suitable for heavy machine learning training or high-performance computing workloads that require raw clock speed.

It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor operating at 2.6 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores. The server is equipped with an extensive 504.0 GB of RAM, providing 31.5 GB per vCPU, alongside 2458 GB of local SSD storage. Benchmark results indicate solid mid-range performance, with a PassMark CPU score of 17846.77 and a Redis SET throughput of 14.55 million operations per second. While its large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 101.42 GB/sec, its 7B LLM prompt processing is relatively weak at 29.58 tokens per second. This configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, such as large databases, in-memory caching, and enterprise applications requiring high RAM-to-vCPU ratios and local SSD storage.
